STEP 1 - Scene: An airline-style tray meal with roast chicken and stir-fried noodles, plus a juice glass and a chocolate bar. Only the two plated foods are counted.

STEP 2 - Vessel: The noodle plate is a side plate of about 20 cm (area ~314 cm²). The chicken sits on a smaller plate of about 14 cm (area ~154 cm²), judged from its width relative to the noodle plate.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) stir-fried noodles with vegetables and some meat bits, (b) roast chicken, mostly dark meat with skin. The juice and chocolate are not plated food and are excluded.

STEP 4 - Area: Noodles cover about 45% of the 20 cm plate (~141 cm²). Chicken covers about 35% of its 14 cm plate (~54 cm²).

STEP 5 - Volume: Noodles 141 cm² × 2 cm ≈ 282 ml. Chicken 54 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 81 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Noodles 282 ml × 0.8 ≈ 226 g. Chicken 81 ml × 0.95 ≈ 77 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Noodles at about 170 kcal/100 g give 226 g → ~384 kcal. Chicken at about 200 kcal/100 g gives 77 g → ~154 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: The plated food totals about 303 g and ~540 kcal. That is plausible for a noodle portion plus a small piece of chicken, and it is well below a fully loaded dinner plate, which is consistent with what is visible.

Total: ~303 g, ~540 kcal (plated items only; juice and chocolate not included).
